cards.title: Uncertainty Quantification via Monte Carlo Simulation
cards.claim: Uncertainty in human dose/exposure predictions should be quantified by integrating uncertainty from all parameter sources using Monte Carlo simulation. Parameters are assigned distributions (e.g., log-normal) rather than point estimates alone. This approach allows communication of the probability of achieving target exposures despite parameter uncertainty.
conditions: Applicable when point estimates are insufficient to convey risk.
Requires defined distributions for key PK/PD parameters (e.g., CL, Vss, KD, koff).
No correlations between parameters were assumed in the cited methodological example.
required_inputs: Point estimates for all PK/PD parameters.
Defined probability distributions (e.g., log-normal) for each uncertain parameter.
Target exposure metric (e.g., Cmax, AUC, or receptor occupancy threshold).
limitations: Methodological example from SUP011 is for a different drug; it does not provide target-drug parameter values.
Uncertainty in translation (species differences) is a major source of error; human PK uncertainty dominates if animal data is limited.
Does not validate the model; only quantifies uncertainty given the model structure.
cards.downstream_use: Generate empirical distributions of predicted human dose or exposure to support risk assessment and decision-making under uncertainty.
cards.retrieval_keywords: Required inputs and scenario status of prospective human regimen simulation

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
